summary: Demo focused on edge cases: long context windows, high TPS load, streaming backpressure, and timeout behaviors. Covered API surface, Console observability (Optimize recommendations), routing/fallbacks, and SSO/SOC2 concerns. Agreed next steps: share benchmarks, run targeted perf test, and schedule pilot sizing call.
topics: Long context handling (KV cache / prefix caching)
Timeouts, retries, and graceful degradation policies
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Chen from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Priya Nair, our SE. We'll run through a focused demo: long context, high TPS, streaming backpressure and timeouts.
[00:18] John (NimbusPay - CTO): Hey Alex, thanks. We're mostly concerned about a few production gotchas — we have some payment reconciliation flows that need 75k token contexts sometimes and bursts to 1k TPS during batch windows.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): Got it. We'll show the API, Console traces, and Optimize suggestions. Quick qualifier — are you leaning Hosted or Dedicated for the pilot?
[00:48] Sophie (Product): Likely Dedicated, but we'd like to validate cost and latency first. Also interested in streaming for UX.
[01:02] Maya (SRE): Security-wise SOC2 and KMS integration are musts. We also need audit logs.
[01:15] Alex: That's standard. Redwood Private and Dedicated both support KMS/HSM and audit logs. We'll attach compliance docs after.
[01:28] Priya: Ok jumping into the API. (voice overlays) So here's a long-context demo — we attach a 60k token context, show prefix caching / KV cache hits. Note: transcription may flip some names — sorry if something sounds off.
[01:45] [screen share noises] Priya: Sending request now... The first call is cold, we see KV warm-up in the Console trace. Latency initially spikes to ~700ms on token 1, then steady state per-token latency is ~12ms.
[02:10] Ethan (ML Eng): Quick q — are those microsecond-level or wall-clock per-token?
[02:18] Priya: Wall-clock per-token on a p4-like profile; on Dedicated you'd see slightly different numbers depending on quantization and kernel selection.
[02:30] [00:02:30] Alex: We should call out that kernel selection and quantization can change throughput/latency tradeoffs. Optimize will suggest quantization for these sequences.
[02:45] John: For our 75k token sessions — what about memory/kv overflow?
[02:52] Priya: We show two strategies: prefix trimming and offloading older KV pages to slower storage, plus automatic shard routing. Console shows warning when KV cache exceeds threshold. There's also a fallback to shorter context models if strict SLOs are required.
[03:15] [00:03:15] Priya: Now we're simulating high TPS bursts — sending 1200 concurrent small requests to emulate your batch windows. Watch the Console: request queue length, batching statistics, and backpressure signals.
[03:35] [typing noises] Priya: First scenario: Hosted with autoscaling. We see autoscaler kick, latency distribution shifts right briefly, then stabilizes. Backpressure appears as 429s for a narrow window because of throttling policy.
[03:53] Maya: 429s are a hard no for some of our endpoints, can you retry gracefully?
[04:00] Priya: Yes — Redwood supports client retry policies and internal queuing; plus you can set per-route fallback to a cheaper model or cached response. The SDK includes idempotency keys and exponential backoff out of the box.
[04:22] Alex: Also we surface the per-token cost impact in the Console so product teams can see tradeoffs.
[04:30] [00:04:30] Priya: Now streaming. We're streaming a large completion back to the client; on the network we introduce artificial backpressure (simulate slow client). You'll notice the server will buffer up to configured bytes, then apply windowing and pause sending. If the client is too slow for too long, the server will checkpoint the KV state and continue processing but mark the stream as partial and emit an event in the trace.
[04:58] John: If a client disconnects mid-stream, can we resume?
[05:04] Priya: We have a resume token pattern in the API: the server can offer a resume_id and KV snapshot if the model run is resumable for that session. There are some model-specific constraints; not all are resumable beyond KV limits.
[05:20] Sophie: How about timeouts? We have strict 2s frontend timeouts for some requests.
[05:28] Priya: For strict 2s paths we recommend pre-warming or using a smaller context model, aggressive prefix caching, and setting a hard cutoff in the call that returns partial results. Console can set SLO alarms for these routes.
[05:45] [00:05:45] Alex: On the pilot: for Dedicated we size based on peak TPS and long-context memory. We'll propose a commit level that covers 95th percentile and provide burst capacity for sudden spikes.
[06:02] Ethan: Any notes on streaming backpressure causing memory leaks or runaway queues?
[06:09] Priya: In our testing we add backpressure signals that throttle producers and apply circuit-breakers; Console shows queue depth metrics and we have auto-prune for stalled streams. If a stream is stalled beyond threshold, the runtime gracefully cancels and emits an event for post-mortem.
[06:30] [00:06:30] John: Competitors like Anthropic, OpenAI — how do you compare for high-TPS pricing?
[06:40] Alex: We show unit economics in the spreadsheet, but Redwood's intelligent batching and KV cache often reduce per-token cost significantly at scale vs raw per-token APIs. Also the Dedicated model offers committed capacity and predictable per-request cost.
[06:58] Priya: Back to the Console — here's an Optimize suggestion: switch to 4-bit quant for this model variant to cut inference cost ~30% with minor latency increase; route lower-criticality traffic to a cheaper variant automatically during peaks.
[07:18] Maya: How deterministic are outputs after quantization? We care about regression.
[07:24] Priya: Optimize also hooks into evals and can run regression checks against a golden prompt set; alerts trigger if ROUGE/whatever metric changes beyond threshold. We'll show that in the pilot.
[07:40] [00:07:40] Alex: Security briefly — SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS, and audit logs are all supported. For Private deployments we can provide on-prem images and VPC peering.
[07:55] John: Good. Our legal team will want SOC2 and contract language.
[08:00] Alex: We'll attach SOC2 report and the security whitepaper.
[08:08] [00:08:08] Priya: Now a rough live perf check: simulating mixed long and short requests. You can see the per-route breakdown and token-level latency heatmap. There's some transcription artifacts here — but the main point is the heatmap highlights cold-start hotspots.
[08:30] Sophie: Are there observability hooks for our internal tracing?
[08:36] Priya: Yes, we support trace correlation via trace_id headers, and you can ingest Redwood traces into your datadog/tempo via exporters.
[08:48] Ethan: Curious about timeout strategies for streaming — should we chunk at application-level?
[08:54] Priya: We recommend chunking at semantic boundaries and using the SDK's streaming iterator which handles reconnect and resume tokens. The Console shows drop-off points where clients commonly disconnect.
[09:10] [00:09:10] Alex: Walkthrough of fallback policies: model variants, regional routing, and graceful degrade to cached responses. You can set percent-based rollouts in the Console for canaries.
[09:28] John: For our pilot, SLA is 99.9 for latency under 200ms P50 for simple prompts — realistic?
[09:36] Priya: For small prompts and Dedicated yes. For long-context requests P50 will be higher, we recommend separate route and SLOs. We'll size to meet your percentile targets for defined route categories.
[09:55] [00:09:55] Alex: Let's capture the edge-case items we discussed: resume tokens, backpressure behavior, timeouts and partial results, kv cache limits and offload, optimize quantization/regression tests, and dedicated sizing.
[10:15] Maya: One more: how do you instrument streaming backpressure events for post-mortem?
[10:21] Priya: The Console emits stream_event logs; you'll get a stream timeline with backpressure markers, client RTT, and buffer occupancy. Those are searchable via the logs UI.
[10:40] John: Ok this is helpful. Any gotchas - like hidden costs when you enable Resume or KV offloading?
[10:48] Alex: Offloading may incur storage IO costs; resume tokens store metadata. We'll call those out in the pricing sheet.
[11:02] [00:11:02] Priya: Demoing the Optimize suggestions for batching: here we recommend batch window of 10ms for this workload to maximize throughput without increasing tail latency during bursts. Console sim hits show reduced token cost.
[11:20] Ethan: Can we set route-level hard timeouts and a fallback response?
[11:26] Priya: Yes, per-route timeout+fallback is supported; you can return cached summaries if a call times out.
[11:40] Sophie: For regulatory reasons we might need data residency. Is that supported?
[11:45] Alex: Yes, Redwood Private with region pinning or VPC deployment supports data residency. We'll include architecture notes.
[12:02] [00:12:02] John: Ok, let's talk pilot scope — we want a 4-week pilot, run a sim that covers long contexts and 1k TPS burst tests. Can Redwood run that or do we run in our environment?
[12:14] Priya: We can run both — Redwood can run a controlled perf run against Dedicated staging and you can run a client-side test. We'll compare traces and KV metrics.
[12:28] Alex: We'll size Dedicated reservation to cover 95th percentile and include burst capacity. Pricing sheet will show commit vs burst delta.
[12:40] Maya: Who signs off on success? Our stakeholders include Product, SRE, and Legal.
[12:46] John: We'll sign off on latency and correctness metrics plus security checks.
[12:55] [00:12:55] Alex: Great. Quick run of Q&A from the team — Sophie: any additional concerns?
[13:02] Sophie: No, mainly UX.
[13:05] [00:13:05] Priya: There's a short note on streaming limits — some older open models don't support resume; we mark those in the model catalog. Also model-specific behavior around KV clearing; Console annotations call that out.
[13:24] Ethan: If we switch quantization mid-pilot could outputs shift? Need regression alerts.
[13:30] Priya: Yes, Optimize will run regression checks on your golden prompt set before recommending production cutover.
[13:45] John: Can we get a copy of the demo trace?
[13:49] Alex: Yes, we'll export and share the trace and logs.
[13:55] [00:13:55] Priya: Final recap: we'll send pricing + benchmark spreadsheet, schedule perf run, NimbusPay sends request distribution, and we'll reconvene week of 11/24 for sizing.
[14:10] Maya: Thanks all, helpful session.
[14:15] Alex: Thanks folks — we'll follow up.
[14:20] [END]
